title: Agricultural Field Assistant: Resolve an Uncertain Sample Label
prompt: You are a field assistant in a fictional crop-research trial. Two sealed sample bags arrive at the collection desk. Bag labels say Plot 8 and Plot 9, but the collection sheet repeats Plot 8 twice. A colleague suggests correcting the second row to Plot 9 because it seems obvious. Exercise policy says uncertain sample identity must be logged and held separately; only the trial coordinator can resolve the link using original collection records. Explain how you would protect the samples and hand over the discrepancy. Do not open bags, infer crop condition, or give field-treatment instructions.
blurb: Preserve sample identity uncertainty so a plausible correction cannot corrupt a crop trial.

rubric.label: Recognize the missing link
rubric.description: Separates bag labels from proven plot origin.

anchors.0: Changes the second row to Plot 9 because there are two bags.
anchors.2: Identifies the mismatch and leaves both origins unverified.
anchors.4: Records both bag labels and the duplicate sheet entry, explains that labels alone do not establish the collection link, and avoids assuming which item is wrong.

rubric.label: Keep the samples and records traceable
rubric.description: Applies the supplied hold process without altering evidence.

anchors.0: Relabels, mixes, opens, or discards a sample.
anchors.2: Holds the sealed bags separately and retains the sheet.
anchors.4: Uses temporary hold references without replacing original labels, records arrival context, and keeps physical and record evidence together for the coordinator's investigation.

rubric.label: Support an accountable resolution
rubric.description: Names what can establish identity and who decides.

anchors.0: Releases results under a guessed plot ID or treats a colleague's hunch as approval.
anchors.2: Contacts the trial coordinator and asks for the original records.
anchors.4: Hands over the exact conflict, collector/time evidence if available, and pending status; requires a documented coordinator decision or an explicit unresolved classification before trial analysis.

reference.scenario: You are a field assistant in a fictional crop-research trial. Two sealed sample bags arrive at the collection desk. Bag labels say Plot 8 and Plot 9, but the collection sheet repeats Plot 8 twice. A colleague suggests correcting the second row to Plot 9 because it seems obvious. Exercise policy says uncertain sample identity must be logged and held separately; only the trial coordinator can resolve the link using original collection records. Explain how you would protect the samples and hand over the discrepancy. Do not open bags, infer crop condition, or give field-treatment instructions.

facts.value: The collection sheet lists collector M and time 09:40. The original field notebook is with the trial coordinator; no photograph or map link is present at the desk.
A designated sample-hold shelf is available. The coordinator can inspect the notebook this afternoon; no sample-storage requirements beyond the supplied hold instruction are provided.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about containment or timing

model_points: The duplicate sheet entry and different bag labels produce an identity question, not proof of which record is wrong. A plausible rewrite could create a false trial result.
Preserve sealed bags and original records with distinct temporary hold references. Do not invent storage temperatures, chemical hazards, or treatment instructions.
The coordinator can use original collection evidence. If identity remains unresolved, the trial must represent that uncertainty rather than assigning a convenient plot.

probes.trigger: candidate assumes the bag labeled Plot 9 resolves the duplicate
probes.question: What links that label to the actual collection event?

probes.trigger: candidate proposes excluding both samples from analysis
probes.question: Who should decide that disposition, and what evidence would you preserve for them?

probes.trigger: candidate first changes the sheet then realizes the link is uncertain
probes.question: How would you disclose and trace the correction without hiding the original entry?

fair_alternatives: A temporary hold identifier or an evidence table can keep the two bags distinct without overwriting original labels.
Unresolved identity may ultimately justify exclusion, but the coordinator owns the documented disposition under the exercise policy.

Assess the work demonstrated here. Accept relevant examples from education, volunteering, caregiving, placements, or paid work; professional vocabulary and employer pedigree are not evidence of a stronger answer.
reference.assessment_limits: Assess research-sample traceability and field-team communication. Do not assess crop diagnosis, sample-storage science, pesticide handling, or real agricultural operating procedures. Unobserved dimensions are not failures. Credit a reasoned correction and distinguish independently demonstrated reasoning from coached assistance. Do not penalize a candidate for an unrevealed conditional fact; credit appropriate requests and conditional plans, and distinguish candidate assumptions from interviewer-supplied evidence.

interviewer_notes: Assess research-sample traceability and field-team communication. Do not assess crop diagnosis, sample-storage science, pesticide handling, or real agricultural operating procedures. Use only the supplied fictional facts and policies; acknowledge unknowns. Ask one triggered probe at a time after the candidate has finished. Accept plain language and accessible written or spoken explanations. Do not score accent, typing speed, confidence, credentials, or experience with a named employer. Credit revisions and record assistance. All participants are fictional adults; no real patient, client, operational, or confidential data is needed. Allow silence for thinking without treating it as failure. In short sessions prioritize the core decision and one material follow-up, leaving room for a correction and wrap-up.

learning_drills.title: Write a sample-identity hold
learning_drills.prompt: Write a short hold note listing bag labels, sheet entries, available provenance, unresolved link, and coordinator action. This is self-guided practice; no model assessment is performed.
checklist: Do not equate a label with verified origin
Keep the original duplicate entry visible
